C2S-R.name: Reachability
C2S-R.statement: Traffic from router r can be delivered to destination prefix p in every environment allowed by the chosen failure model.
C2S-R.parameters: r, p; fixed-up links, fixed-down links, symbolic links; failure bound k
C2S-R.interpretation: Mine the router/prefix instances that satisfy the predicate. Do not assume that every router must reach every prefix. The evaluation uses k = 1, 2, 3 with all links eligible to fail.

C2S-I.name: Destination isolation
C2S-I.statement: Traffic from router r cannot be delivered to prefix p in any environment allowed by the chosen failure model.
C2S-I.parameters: r, p and the failure model
C2S-I.interpretation: Isolation is absence of delivery. A mined isolation fact can describe an accidental outage as well as an intended filter; intent needs a separate specification.

C2S-W.name: Waypoint traversal
C2S-W.statement: Traffic from r toward p traverses the nominated router w under the chosen failure model.
C2S-W.parameters: r, p, w and the failure model
C2S-W.interpretation: The waypoint must be nominated or mined from the candidate router set. Fix the forwarding and ECMP path quantifiers before translating the predicate to Lean, ASP, or Datalog.

C2S-L.name: Multiple forwarding paths
C2S-L.statement: Traffic from r toward p can use at least two forwarding paths under the chosen failure model.
C2S-L.parameters: r, p and the failure model
C2S-L.interpretation: The requirement concerns path multiplicity. It does not establish equal byte rates, independent failure domains, or link-disjoint paths.

DNA-R.name: Reachability additions and removals
DNA-R.statement: Compute each source/destination/packet-class reachability fact gained or lost between a base configuration and an update.
DNA-R.parameters: ordered base/update pair; source and destination edge ports; packet equivalence class
DNA-R.interpretation: An added or removed fact is a behavioral difference. Calling the difference a violation requires a separate list of permitted changes. Differential reachability is implemented in the evaluated prototype.

DNA-W.name: Waypoint changes
DNA-W.statement: Compute the waypoint-traversal facts gained or lost by an update for a specified source, destination, packet class, and waypoint.
DNA-W.parameters: ordered base/update pair; edge ports; packet class; waypoint
DNA-W.interpretation: The paper describes the predicate and illustrates differential waypointing. The evaluated prototype centers on reachability; the presence of configurations does not establish a waypoint result.

DNA-L.name: Forwarding-path-count changes
DNA-L.statement: Compute changes in the number of forwarding paths for a source/destination/packet class across an update.
DNA-L.parameters: ordered base/update pair; edge ports; packet class; path count n
DNA-L.interpretation: The paper illustrates changes from n paths to a different count. Treat the predicate as a paper-defined extension, not a claim that all local runs measured load balancing.

DNA-F.name: Reachability under individual link failures
DNA-F.statement: For each eligible link, compare all-pairs reachability before and after disabling that link.
DNA-F.parameters: baseline snapshot; edge-port pairs; packet classes; one failed link per comparison
DNA-F.interpretation: The experiment enumerates failures and reports changed reachability. The experiment does not assert that all pairs survive every single failure.

SRE-R.name: Reachability
SRE-R.statement: For each selected source s, destination d, and packet class p, determine the failure states in which p can reach d from s.
SRE-R.parameters: s, d, p; link/node failure variables
SRE-R.interpretation: The result is a condition on failures. A universal guarantee requires restricting that condition to a declared failure model.

SRE-I.name: Destination isolation
SRE-I.statement: Determine the failure states in which packets in p sent from s cannot reach d.
SRE-I.interpretation: Isolation means no delivery. It is different from NetDice's link-sharing isolation between several flows.

SRE-W.name: Waypoint reachability
SRE-W.statement: Determine the failure states in which packets in p can reach d from s along a path through w.
SRE-W.parameters: s, d, p, w; failure model; ECMP path quantifier
SRE-W.interpretation: The paper constructs the waypoint condition by combining qualifying forwarding paths. An assertion that every ECMP path must cross w needs an explicit all-paths formulation. SRE's mining and single-flow checking code use different combinations of qualifying and nonqualifying paths.

SRE-L.name: Load balancing over n routes
SRE-L.statement: Determine when packets in p can reach d from s using n forwarding routes.
SRE-L.parameters: s, d, p, n; route-count semantics
SRE-L.interpretation: The local mining implementation checks for at least two alternatives and leaves disjoint-path handling as a TODO. Neither equal traffic volume nor disjoint paths follows from the path count.

SRE-T.name: Reachability failure tolerance
SRE-T.statement: Find the largest k for which the chosen reachability predicate holds whenever at most k eligible links fail.
SRE-T.parameters: one reachability instance; eligible links; environment constraints
SRE-T.interpretation: A tolerance of 0 allows the all-up state but fails under some single-link outage. A value of −1 means that the predicate already fails with all links up.

SRE-TW.name: Waypoint failure tolerance
SRE-TW.statement: Find the largest k for which the chosen waypoint predicate survives every allowed failure of at most k links.
SRE-TW.parameters: one waypoint instance and its path quantifier; eligible links
SRE-TW.interpretation: Use the waypoint predicate itself, not just endpoint connectivity. A surviving alternate path can bypass the waypoint.

SRE-TI.name: Isolation failure tolerance
SRE-TI.statement: Find the largest k for which the chosen no-delivery predicate survives every allowed failure of at most k links.
SRE-TI.interpretation: Failure can redirect traffic around a filter. Isolation in the all-up state alone does not establish failure-tolerant isolation.

SRE-PR.name: Reachability probability
SRE-PR.statement: Compute the probability that a selected reachability predicate holds under a declared distribution of failures.
SRE-PR.interpretation: The WAN comparison uses link failure probability 0.001 and node failure probability 0.0001. Node failures correlate incident link failures. Those benchmark numbers are not measured reliability or a required SLA.

SRE-PW.name: Waypoint probability
SRE-PW.statement: Compute the probability that a selected waypoint predicate holds under a declared distribution of failures.
SRE-PW.parameters: waypoint instance; path quantifier; joint failure distribution
SRE-PW.interpretation: The paper compares probability queries with NetDice at an imprecision target of 0.0001. A historical result file does not by itself bind every distribution or routing assumption used in that run.

SRE-DR.name: Reachability changes under failures
SRE-DR.statement: Find the packet/failure combinations for which reachability differs between two selected snapshots.
SRE-DR.parameters: ordered snapshot pair; matched endpoints; packet classes; failure bound
SRE-DR.interpretation: Compare the same environment on both sides. The BICS experiment includes k = 0 and k = 3; a no-failure comparison can miss a change exposed by an outage.

SRE-DT.name: Changes in reachability failure tolerance
SRE-DT.statement: Compute the change in each selected reachability instance's link-failure tolerance between two snapshots.
SRE-DT.parameters: ordered snapshot pair; common endpoint and failure interpretation
SRE-DT.interpretation: A decrease is evidence of reduced modeled resilience. Whether the decrease is authorized remains a separate policy question.

SRE-DP.name: Changes in reachability probability
SRE-DP.statement: Compute the change in each selected reachability instance's probability between two snapshots under the same failure distribution.
SRE-DP.parameters: ordered snapshot pair; reachability instance; common joint distribution
SRE-DP.interpretation: Do not attribute a probability change solely to configurations if the distribution also changed.

CAMPUS-R.name: Access-VLAN reachability changes
CAMPUS-R.statement: Compare reachability between access VLANs across explicitly selected campus snapshots, respecting their VRFs and ACLs.
CAMPUS-R.source: SRE §8.7, PDF p. 12; DNA §8.2, PDF pp. 11–12
CAMPUS-R.parameters: ordered campus snapshots; access VLAN/VRF identities; traffic classes
CAMPUS-R.interpretation: The local collection contains more dataset directories than the paper's 67 snapshots. Nested snapshots and alternate representations remain separate. Directory names alone do not prove a chronological experiment sequence.

CAMPUS-T.name: Core-to-access-VLAN single-failure reachability
CAMPUS-T.statement: Test whether each designated core router can reach each access VLAN despite any one eligible link failure.
CAMPUS-T.parameters: mapping of paper cores C1/C2 to local devices; access VLANs; eligible links; traffic class
CAMPUS-T.interpretation: The paper reports tolerance 1 for its core-to-VLAN checks. The local names do not establish the C1/C2 mapping, and the reported result has not been reproduced on these files.

ND-R.name: Reachability probability
ND-R.statement: Compute the probability that a selected flow is delivered to its destination.
ND-R.source: NetDice §3.4–3.5, Table 1, PDF p. 5; SRE §8.2, PDF p. 10
ND-R.parameters: source, destination prefix, external announcements, BGP roles, failure distribution
ND-R.interpretation: A graph alone does not determine delivery. The synthesized routing environment and the failure distribution are part of the query.

ND-W.name: Waypoint probability
ND-W.statement: Compute the probability that a selected flow traverses a selected waypoint.
ND-W.source: NetDice §3.4–3.5, Table 1, PDF p. 5; §8.2, PDF pp. 10–11
ND-W.parameters: source, destination prefix, waypoint, routing environment, failure distribution
ND-W.interpretation: The main WAN experiment chooses waypoints and flows for synthetic trials. Keep each recorded trial's router roles and query together; the trials are not operator requirements.

ND-E.name: Egress probability
ND-E.statement: Compute the probability that a flow exits through a nominated egress router.
ND-E.parameters: source, destination, required egress, routing environment, failure distribution
ND-E.interpretation: The property is supported by the paper. Most collected inputs provide no nominated egress or corresponding recorded trial.

ND-P.name: Exact path-length probability
ND-P.statement: Compute the probability that a flow traverses exactly l links.
ND-P.parameters: source, destination, exact link count l, routing environment, failure distribution
ND-P.interpretation: An exact length differs from an upper bound. The SRE helper compares stored path-list size; check whether that representation counts nodes or links before using it as a NetDice-equivalent checker.

ND-B.name: Traffic-load balance probability
ND-B.statement: Compute the probability that the loads on a nominated set of links differ by no more than a chosen amount Δ.
ND-B.parameters: several flows and their volumes; link set; Δ; traffic splitting; failure distribution
ND-B.interpretation: Topology and ECMP path counts alone cannot instantiate the query. Traffic volumes and the allowed imbalance must be supplied.

ND-I.name: Flow link-disjointness probability
ND-I.statement: Compute the probability that the selected flows use no common links.
ND-I.parameters: flow set; routing environment; forwarding/splitting semantics; failure distribution
ND-I.interpretation: The flows can each be reachable. The isolation condition concerns shared links, not blocked communication between endpoints.

ND-C.name: Congestion-threshold probability
ND-C.statement: Compute the probability that the combined traffic of selected flows on one link stays at or below threshold t.
ND-C.source: NetDice §3.4–3.5, Table 1, PDF p. 5; §8.4, PDF pp. 11–12
ND-C.parameters: flows, volumes, monitored link, threshold t, traffic splitting, failure distribution
ND-C.interpretation: AS-3549 retains explicit congestion trial strings, including volumes and threshold 500. Their symbolic destinations and source-label mapping still need resolution. Other topology-only datasets generally lack those parameters.

EX-L.name: Route-leak freedom
EX-L.statement: Forbid propagation of a route learned from a noncustomer neighbor to another noncustomer neighbor where the declared relationship policy disallows transit.
EX-L.parameters: external-neighbor relationships; symbolic advertisement space; permitted transit policy
EX-L.interpretation: The common runner checks route leaks. Accurate customer/peer/provider classification is required; a BGP neighbor address or AS number alone does not establish a commercial relationship.

EX-R.name: Route-hijack freedom
EX-R.statement: Prevent an external advertisement from becoming the selected route for a prefix designated as internal.
EX-R.parameters: authoritative internal-prefix set; external advertisements; routing abstractions
EX-R.interpretation: An interface subnet is evidence of addressing, not automatically the complete protected-prefix policy. Prefix ownership must be declared before universal checking.

EX-T.name: Traffic-hijack freedom
EX-T.statement: Prevent traffic destined for designated internal prefixes from being forwarded out of the internal network.
EX-T.parameters: internal ingress points and prefixes; external exits; modeled advertisements
EX-T.interpretation: The predicate concerns forwarding. Route selection alone is insufficient because next-hop resolution and the forwarding path also matter.

EX-B.name: BlockToExternal
EX-B.statement: Prevent export to external neighbors of routes carrying the policy's block-to-external designation.
EX-B.source: Expresso §6.3, PDF p. 9; §7.3, Table 4, PDF p. 11; Bagpipe §3, PDF p. 7
EX-B.parameters: internal/external boundary; BTE community and its policy semantics; external advertisements
EX-B.interpretation: Internet2 defines BLOCK-TO-EXTERNAL as community 11537:888 in the collected JSON. The paper reports four Expresso violations and five Bagpipe violations with different recognized neighbor counts. Those are historical results, not results of this extraction.

EX-E.name: Egress preference
EX-E.statement: Select the preferred external egress according to a declared ordering whenever the relevant choices are available.
EX-E.parameters: destination class; ordered egress preferences; eligible advertisements
EX-E.interpretation: No complete operator-supplied ordering is bundled with the collected datasets. Route-policy settings can suggest an ordering but do not independently specify the intended one.

EX-FL.name: Forwarding-loop freedom
EX-FL.statement: Ensure that modeled packets do not revisit a forwarding node indefinitely.
EX-FL.parameters: packet classes; ingress points; symbolic routing/forwarding environment
EX-FL.interpretation: The repository contains a loop checker. The common routing-only runner does not execute every forwarding checker.

EX-FB.name: Forwarding-blackhole freedom
EX-FB.statement: Ensure that traffic expected to be delivered does not terminate at an unintended forwarding dead end.
EX-FB.parameters: intended delivery classes and endpoints; allowed drops; forwarding environment
EX-FB.interpretation: Specify permitted ACL drops and unknown destinations first. Not every dropped packet is a policy violation.

BP-M.name: NoMartian
BP-M.statement: Ensure that a route for a designated martian prefix is unavailable in the selected local BGP RIB.
BP-M.parameters: martian-prefix predicate; internal routers; allowed BGP traces
BP-M.interpretation: The formal predicate constrains the selected local route. It should not be strengthened into a claim that a router never receives such an advertisement. The paper also evaluates a separately modified configuration with sanity checks removed; that variant is not identified in this collection.

BP-G.name: Internet2's refined Gao-Rexford preference
BP-G.statement: Select routes according to Internet2's relationship and community-dependent ranking while retaining its invalid-prefix restrictions.
BP-G.parameters: manually classified customers/peers; valid prefixes; ranking rules including HIGH_PEERS
BP-G.interpretation: The paper's refinement allows community-dependent preferences and has no provider neighbors. A generic customer-over-peer assertion would lose that refinement. The collected JSON lacks the paper's complete classification and formal ranking specification.
